content.user_title: Manage the Full Data Asset Lifecycle
content.value_statement: Data asset programs often lack connected policies, ownership, workflows, and measurable controls. This skill designs a practical lifecycle system from planning through disposal and oversight.
actual_capabilities: Assesses data asset management maturity across four defined levels.
Designs governance roles, responsibilities, policies, and decision structures.
Maps planning, formation, registration, use, disposal, and oversight workflows.
Drafts a core management policy and supporting specialist policy outlines.
Defines measurable indicators for asset scale, returns, use, registration, and compliance.
Creates phased implementation plans, deliverable lists, and quality checks.
limitations: It does not provide binding legal, accounting, valuation, or regulatory opinions.
Its four-level maturity model is an internal framework, not an official certification.
Current policy references and local requirements must be verified before implementation.
Useful recommendations require accurate details about assets, entities, systems, and responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Assess governance maturity
use_cases.description: Evaluate current policies, registers, roles, and controls. Produce a prioritized path from fragmented practices to a managed system.

use_cases.title: Build a policy framework
use_cases.description: Design a core data asset policy with focused rules for ownership, quality, cost, registers, operations, security, and disposal.

use_cases.title: Create performance controls
use_cases.description: Define indicators, data owners, collection methods, review frequency, and reporting templates for ongoing management.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic maturity check
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess our data asset management maturity. We have [policies], [register status], [responsible team], and [current activities]. Identify our level and three priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Design the governance structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design governance for [organization type] with [business units]. Define decision, management, and execution roles. Include responsibilities, escalation paths, and meeting cadence.

prompt_templates.title: Create a lifecycle implementation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased plan covering planning, formation, registration, use, disposal, and oversight. For each phase, specify owners, inputs, outputs, controls, and timing.

prompt_templates.title: Build an integrated control framework
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an integrated data asset framework for [organization]. Connect policies, workflows, registers, financial records, performance indicators, audits, and disposal approvals. State assumptions and gaps.

output_examples.input: We have completed accounting recognition, but we have no asset register, policy, or designated owner.
output: Priority 1: appoint a responsible department and named owner.
Priority 2: establish a data asset register linked to financial records.
Priority 3: issue a core management policy with review and disposal controls.

output_examples.input: Design a data asset governance structure for a group with five subsidiaries.
output_examples.output: The group sets policy, standards, indicators, and consolidated oversight. Each subsidiary maintains its register, executes controls, and reports changes quarterly.

output_examples.input: Create measurable indicators for our quarterly data asset review.
output: Asset scale: recognized and managed assets by legal entity.
Use rate: active assets divided by available assets.
Return rate: attributable income divided by the defined asset base.
Registration completion: registered assets divided by assets requiring registration.
Compliance rate: compliant reviewed items divided by all reviewed items.

best_practices: Confirm the legal entity, objectives, and asset scope before designing controls.
Assign one accountable owner, one required output, and one deadline to every lifecycle step.
Verify policy citations, accounting treatments, and local requirements with qualified specialists.
anti_patterns: Do not treat accounting recognition as a complete lifecycle management system.
Do not create policies without owners, operating procedures, records, and review mechanisms.
Do not pursue advanced monetization before ownership, compliance, quality, and registration controls are ready.

faq.question: What lifecycle stages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers planning, formation, registration, use, disposal, and continuous oversight and evaluation.

faq.question: Can it assess our current maturity?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses a four-level internal model based on policies, registers, ownership, process closure, value creation, and performance management.

faq.question: Can it draft governance policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft a core management policy and specialist policy outlines tailored to your stated context.

faq.question: Does it replace legal or accounting advice?
faq.answer: No. Qualified professionals must validate legal rights, accounting treatment, valuation, tax, and regulatory conclusions.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide objectives, legal entities, asset inventory, existing policies, responsible teams, systems, registers, financial links, known gaps, and deadlines.

faq.question: Can small organizations use the framework?
faq.answer: Yes. A small organization can begin with one policy, one register, one accountable owner, and a limited set of controls.
